summary.headline: Tipco FY26 total income rose 9.5% to INR146 crore, with H2 income up 66% to INR95 crore and PAT up 65% to INR25.31 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) as its first earnings call after the BSE SME listing on 1 April 2026. Total income was INR146 crore versus INR133 crore, and H2 income reached INR95 crore against INR57 crore in the corresponding period. EBITDA rose 62% to INR38.9 crore, with margin at 26.63% versus 17.95%, and PAT rose 65% to INR25.31 crore with a 17.32% margin. Management guided to Pune plant contributing toward INR180 crore total revenue in FY27, with 25% capacity in FY27, 75% in FY28, and full capacity in about two years. Debtor days rose sharply from 72 to 169, which management attributed to higher H2 sales.

segments.name: Industrial process equipment (mills, dispersers, homogenisers, turnkey projects)
segments.commentary: Core business serving paint, inks, coatings, pharma, cosmetics and food processing. Management says capacity utilisation is about 80%. Turnkey and equipment-plus-engineering offering cited as a differentiator.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Lab machine priced around INR36 lakh for up to 200 litre fuel batch, first order from HEMRL/DRDO. Approvals obtained from DRDO and HEMRL; one machine sold to a defence-linked buyer after trial. Applications cited include nano-dispersion of rocket fuel and solid-state battery R&D.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export business grew over the last two years; Gulf and African markets added, with European tie-up planned for expansion into the EU. No export revenue split was given.

guidance_outlook: Pune facility expected to be about 25% operational in FY27, about 75% in FY28, and 100% in about two years.
Management estimates INR180 crore plus total revenue in FY27 including Pune and existing locations.
Pune capex estimated at INR40 crore (land, building, machinery), plus about INR20 crore for existing-facility expansion, totalling about INR60 crore.
Funding model: about 75% bank term loan and 25% from internal margin; working capital limits to be used for working capital.
Long-term aspiration of top line above INR1,000 crore, per the Chairman, with no timeline given.
FY28 guidance to be provided after H1 FY27 results; only FY27 projection given.
capex_capacity: Pune facility: new unit under the same company (not a separate entity), with a planned experience centre for customer trials. Focus on cosmetics, adhesives and personal care under LexaMix (Germany) collaboration.
Sonipat, Haryana: current capacity about 80% utilised. Additional land of about 4-5 acres nearby being acquired for expansion.
Pune expected to serve southern and western India, with Sonipat covering north and east.
Pune capex about INR40 crore; total planned expansion about INR60 crore including about INR20 crore for existing facility.
Planned SAP rollout for compliance, audit and internal audit systems in coming months.
demand_pricing: Management says paint and chemical consumption grows at least 10% a year, supporting demand for process equipment.
Pricing positioned between European and Indian peers: management said if German peers sell at 10, Tipco sells at 6; if Indian peers sell at 4, Tipco sells at 6.
Named peers: GMM Pfaudler, Tetra Pak, Bühler, NETZSCH, VIB (international); Praj Industries and Raj Process (domestic).

Top customers cited: Sirca Paints, JK Cement, Asian Paints, MBT (BASF), Robo Street, B.C. Petro Chem, Aaron Industries, Shyam Paint, Berger, UltraTech, JK Maxx, Nerolac (Nerolac seen as a large-order opportunity). No revenue share disclosed.
Order execution: 30-45 days for smaller orders, 3-6 months for larger orders. Current order book about INR60-70 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why does management believe growth will sustain over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a multi-year industrial capex cycle and positioning across Pune expansion, German technology collaboration, exports, defence and higher-value engineering. No quantitative target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the Pune expansion and what products will it make?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects INR180 crore plus total revenue in FY27 including Pune; Pune is focused on cosmetics, adhesives and personal care machinery under the LexaMix collaboration, with higher expected margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debtor days rise from 72 to 169 days?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debtors are mainly private corporates, the rise reflects higher H2 sales, and payments are being realised on time. Inventory fell from INR31 crore to INR21 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the use of cash and borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR48 crore of unutilised IPO funds sits within the INR60 crore cash balance and is being used to clear dues, with working capital limits underutilised. Borrowings of about INR40 crore were not clearly addressed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence opportunity and status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approvals from DRDO and HEMRL are in place, a trial led to one machine purchase, and downstream fuel makers are expected to source from Tipco. Lab machine priced around INR36 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: Are there related-party or governance concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said promoter-group entities operate in separate business lines, related-party transactions are disclosed, and governance steps include SAP rollout and engagement with top six audit firms. No details were given on specific steps taken.

risks_watch: Debtor days rose sharply to 169 from 72; watch collections and working capital in Q1 FY27.
Borrowings of about INR40 crore alongside INR60 crore cash; the use of IPO funds and debt repayment plans need confirmation.
Pune ramp-up (25% in FY27) and INR180 crore FY27 revenue estimate depend on execution and new product acceptance.
Related-party overlap with promoter-group entities; management gave only a qualitative response.
Concentration in paint and coatings customers, and reliance on a limited number of large orders (e.g. cement project in UP).
FY28 guidance deferred until after H1 FY27 results.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, margins and the Pune expansion, but vague and sometimes unstructured on governance, related parties and forward guidance. Many answers were qualitative with no hard figures.
